43442.subject: Financial Accounting
43442.question_text:
Explain the following terms as used in accounting:
(i) Assets
(ii) Liabilities
(iii) Capital
43442.explanation:
(i) Assets: These are resources owned or controlled by a business that provide future economic benefits. Examples include cash, inventory, machinery, and buildings.
(ii) Liabilities: These are obligations of a business to transfer economic resources to other entities. Examples include loans, creditors, and accrued expenses.
(iii) Capital: This represents the owner's equity in the business, calculated as the difference between assets and liabilities. It is the residual interest in the assets of the business after deducting liabilities.

43443.subject: Financial Accounting
43443.question_text:
Using the accounting equation, show how the following transactions affect the financial position of a business:
(i) The owner introduced $5,000 cash as capital.
(ii) Purchased goods worth $2,000 on credit.
(iii) Paid $1,000 to a creditor.
43443.explanation:
The accounting equation is: $Assets = Liabilities + Capital$.
(i) Owner introduced $5,000 cash:
$Assets (Cash) +$5,000 = Liabilities + Capital +$5,000$.
(ii) Purchased goods worth $2,000 on credit:
$Assets (Inventory) +$2,000 = Liabilities (Creditors) +$2,000 + Capital$.
(iii) Paid $1,000 to a creditor:
$Assets (Cash) -$1,000 = Liabilities (Creditors) -$1,000 + Capital$.

43444.subject: Financial Accounting
43444.question_text:
State the double-entry rules for the following accounts:
(i) Assets
(ii) Liabilities
(iii) Income
(iv) Expenses
43444.explanation:
(i) Assets: Debit increases, Credit decreases.
(ii) Liabilities: Debit decreases, Credit increases.
(iii) Income: Debit decreases, Credit increases.
(iv) Expenses: Debit increases, Credit decreases.

43445.subject: Financial Accounting
43445.question_text:
The following information was extracted from the books of Adom Enterprise for the month of June 2018:

Bank Statement Balance as at 30th June, 2018: $12,500 (Dr)
Cash Book Balance as at 30th June, 2018: $10,800 (Cr)
Unpresented cheques: $3,200
Bank charges not recorded in the cash book: $200
Dividend received directly by the bank: $1,500

Prepare a bank reconciliation statement as at 30th June, 2018.
43445.explanation:
Bank Reconciliation Statement as at 30th June, 2018

$Balance as per Cash Book (Cr)$: $10,800
Add: Dividend received by bank: $1,500
$Total$: $12,300
Less: Bank charges: $200
$Adjusted Cash Book Balance$: $12,100

$Balance as per Bank Statement (Dr)$: $12,500
Less: Unpresented cheques: $3,200
$Adjusted Bank Statement Balance$: $9,300

Note: The adjusted balances should match, but in this case, there may be an error in the question or additional unreconciled items.

43446.subject: Financial Accounting
43446.question_text: Explain the purpose of preparing a Trading Account and a Profit and Loss Account in the final accounts of a business.
43446.explanation:
Trading Account: This account is prepared to determine the gross profit or gross loss of a business. It includes the cost of goods sold and sales revenue.
Profit and Loss Account: This account is prepared to determine the net profit or net loss of a business. It includes all operating expenses, non-operating incomes, and expenses, and is derived after the gross profit or loss is calculated.

43447.subject: Financial Accounting
43447.question_text: Which of the following methods of depreciation allocates a fixed percentage of the book value of an asset each year?
43447.explanation: The Reducing Balance Method allocates a fixed percentage of the book value of an asset each year, resulting in higher depreciation charges in the earlier years of the asset's life.

options.text: Sum of the years' digits method

43448.subject: Financial Accounting
43448.question_text: State three differences between a partnership and a sole proprietorship.
43448.explanation:
(1) Ownership: A partnership has two or more owners, while a sole proprietorship has only one owner.
(2) Liability: Partners in a partnership have unlimited liability, whereas the sole proprietor also has unlimited liability but bears it alone.
(3) Profit Sharing: In a partnership, profits are shared according to the partnership agreement, while in a sole proprietorship, the owner takes all profits.

43449.subject: Financial Accounting
43449.question_text:
The following information relates to the Accra Sports Club for the year ended 31st December, 2017:

Subscriptions received during the year: $25,000
Subscriptions in arrears at the beginning of the year: $3,000
Subscriptions in arrears at the end of the year: $2,000
Subscriptions in advance at the beginning of the year: $1,500
Subscriptions in advance at the end of the year: $1,000

Calculate the amount of subscriptions to be shown in the Income and Expenditure Account for the year ended 31st December, 2017.
43449.explanation:
Subscriptions for the Year:
$Subscriptions received$: $25,000
Add: Subscriptions in arrears at the end of the year: $2,000
Less: Subscriptions in arrears at the beginning of the year: $3,000
Less: Subscriptions in advance at the end of the year: $1,000
Add: Subscriptions in advance at the beginning of the year: $1,500

$Total Subscriptions = 25,000 + 2,000 - 3,000 - 1,000 + 1,500 = $24,500$.

43450.subject: Financial Accounting
43450.question_text: Which of the following ratios measures the ability of a company to pay its short-term obligations?
43450.explanation: The Current Ratio measures the ability of a company to pay its short-term obligations by comparing current assets to current liabilities.

43451.subject: Financial Accounting
43451.question_text:
Explain the following methods of valuing inventory:
(i) First-In, First-Out (FIFO)
(ii) Last-In, First-Out (LIFO)
(iii) Weighted Average Cost
43451.explanation:
(i) FIFO: This method assumes that the first items purchased are the first ones sold. Inventory is valued at the most recent purchase prices.
(ii) LIFO: This method assumes that the last items purchased are the first ones sold. Inventory is valued at the earliest purchase prices.
(iii) Weighted Average Cost: This method calculates the average cost of inventory by dividing the total cost of goods available for sale by the total number of units available for sale.
